facts.text: Founded in the early 1600s, Sombrillo grew around farms along the Rio Santa Cruz and a small chapel built by families who followed Don Juan de Oñate.
In 1695, Governor de Vargas granted the Santa Cruz de la Cañada area to sixty‑six families, cementing Spanish presence on New Mexico’s northern frontier.
Today, Sombrillo hosts one of the nation’s largest Sikh communities, centered around the golden‑dome Hacienda de Guru Ram Das Gurdwara.
Homes here often sit on half‑to‑three‑acre lots, featuring pitched metal roofs and earth‑toned stucco typical of Northern New Mexico style.
The village’s small‑scale farmlands and gardens rely on acequias—irrigation ditches fed by the Santa Cruz River—maintaining a traditional farming rhythm.
By the early 1900s, Sombrillo remained a modest rural community focused on subsistence farming, reflecting Hispanic and Pueblo influences.
